text.p: These are the leading stories in the Belgrade press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified them and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Yugoslav President Zoran Lilic says peace and stability in Europe remain country's main objectives after the lifting of sanctions.
- Yugoslav Foreign Minsiter Milan Milutinovic visiting Zagreb today at the invitation of his Croatian counterpart Mate Granic.
- Strike by some divisions of Belgrade Public transport GSP is political in nature and is an attempt to create chaos in the capital, says Belgrade mayor Nebojisa Covic.
- Government commission adopts report of Yugoslav group for succesion of the former Yugoslavia from Brussels talks. The next round of talks scheduled for November 12 and 13.
- Italy is Yugoslavia's biggest trade partner with trade standing at $437.5 million in the first nine months this year. Italian imports are more than double Yugoslavia's exports.
- Post office savings bank to open foreign currency accounts from mid-November.
- Board of directors of Serbian oil industry NIS says measures have been taken for regular supply of the market with diesel fuel for autumn agricultural work and for heating.
- Exports of agricultural products could reach $550 million this year, says Serbian agriculture minister Nedeljko Sipovac.
- Opposition demands to have representatives in electoral commissions in all polling stations where they have candidates. Protest rally planned for today has been cancelled.
- International observers will monitor Yugoslav November 3 elections, says U.S. State Department spokesman.
- Private entrepreneurs will stage a protest in Belgrade on Wednesday over high taxes.
- Montenegro chose German firm for construction and 25-year exploration of Karuc waterworks which will supply the Montenegrin coast with water. -- Belgrade newsroom 381 11 222 42 54
